subproblems.title: Test forms are Lipschitz in the Euclidean coefficient norm (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). For a k-covector β write |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β, the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15. Then there is a real number c ≥ 0 such that |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ x y : Euclid P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y) ≤ c * dist x y
subproblems.natural_proof:
This accepted declaration is reused verbatim (byte-identical frozen type). The proof below proves its exact statement. Source: parent proof, step 1 (uniform continuity of the test form ω, used for the continuity of t ↦ η^ω_t), in Lipschitz form.

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})²)^{1/2}; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on continuous alternating maps and linear maps.

1. Comparison of norms. For a k-covector α on ℝ^P and any I : Fin k → Fin P, |α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j ‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖. There are at most P^k maps I, so |α|² ≤ P^k‖α‖², i.e. |α| ≤ c₀‖α‖ with c₀ := √(P^k) ≥ 0.
2. Derivative bound. ω is C^∞ with compact support. So Dω = fderiv ℝ ω is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence bounded: there is B ≥ 0 with ‖Dω(z)‖ ≤ B for all z (a continuous function with compact support is bounded).
3. Mean value inequality. ℝ^P is convex and ω is differentiable with ‖Dω‖ ≤ B everywhere, so ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ B·‖x − y‖ for all x, y (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le).
4. Conclusion. Apply step 1 to the covector α = ω(x) − ω(y) and use step 3: |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c₀‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ c₀B·dist(x, y). Put c := c₀B ≥ 0. Then |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: |α| ≤ √(P^k)‖α‖ (each coefficient is bounded by the operator norm).
Dω is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some B.
Mean value inequality: ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ B|x − y|; so c := √(P^k)·B works.

subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm toolkit: continuity, triangle inequality, homogeneity, operator-norm bound, radial retraction (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is a constant c > 0 such that, writing |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n and ‖α‖ for the operator norm: (i) α ↦ |α|_E is continuous; (ii) |α + β|_E ≤ |α|_E + |β|_E for all α, β; (iii) |t•α|_E = |t|·|α|_E for all t ∈ ℝ and α; (iv) |α|_E ≤ c·‖α‖ for all α; (v) for all v, b with |b|_E ≤ 1, |(max 1 |v|_E)⁻¹ • v − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + β) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm β) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ c * ‖α‖) ∧ ∀ v b : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm b ≤ 1 → covectorEuclideanNorm ((max 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm v))⁻¹ • v - b) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm (v - b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This accepted declaration is reused verbatim (byte-identical frozen type). The proof below proves its exact statement. Source: parent proof, step 0(a): |·| is a norm on covectors because the coefficient map is linear. It is completed here by the comparison with the operator norm and the radial-retraction estimate.

Notation: ℐ is the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. For an n-covector α on ℝ^P put Φ(α) := (α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}))_{I ∈ ℐ} ∈ ℝ^ℐ, with the Euclidean norm ‖·‖₂ and inner product ⟨·,·⟩. By definition |α|_E = ‖Φ(α)‖₂: the terms with I not strictly increasing are 0. Φ is linear.

1. (i) Each coordinate α ↦ α(e_I) is evaluation at a fixed tuple, which is continuous on continuous alternating maps. So Φ is continuous and |·|_E = ‖·‖₂ ∘ Φ is continuous.
2. (ii) |α + β|_E = ‖Φα + Φβ‖₂ ≤ ‖Φα‖₂ + ‖Φβ‖₂ = |α|_E + |β|_E.
   (iii) |tα|_E = ‖tΦα‖₂ = |t|·|α|_E.
3. (iv) |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j ‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖ and #ℐ ≤ P^n. So |α|_E ≤ √(P^n)·‖α‖ ≤ c‖α‖ with c := √(P^n) + 1 > 0.
4. (v) Let |b|_E ≤ 1 and r := max 1 |v|_E.
   (a) If |v|_E ≤ 1, then r = 1 and both sides are equal.
   (b) Otherwise r = |v|_E > 1. Put x := Φv, y := Φb and u := x/r, so ‖u‖₂ = 1, ‖y‖₂ ≤ 1, Φ(r⁻¹v − b) = u − y and Φ(v − b) = x − y.
   (c) ‖x − y‖² = ‖x − u‖² + ‖u − y‖² + 2⟨x − u, u − y⟩, and ⟨x − u, u − y⟩ = (r − 1)⟨u, u − y⟩ = (r − 1)(1 − ⟨u, y⟩) ≥ 0, since ⟨u, y⟩ ≤ ‖u‖‖y‖ ≤ 1 and r > 1.
   (d) Hence ‖u − y‖₂ ≤ ‖x − y‖₂, i.e. |r⁻¹v − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E. ∎
proof_key_steps: |α|_E is the Euclidean norm of the linear coefficient vector Φ(α).
Continuity, the triangle inequality and homogeneity follow from Φ being continuous linear.
Each coefficient is at most ‖α‖, so |α|_E ≤ (√(P^n)+1)‖α‖.
The radial retraction onto the unit ball does not increase the distance to points b with |b|_E ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X) when |ω| ≤ c (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(X) ≠ ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and c ∈ ℝ with c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X)^ℝ, where M(X)^ℝ := M(X).toReal. Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → X.mass ≠ ∞ → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |X ω| ≤ c * X.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
This accepted declaration is reused verbatim (byte-identical frozen type). The proof below proves its exact statement. Source: parent proof, step 0(b) (|T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖, via admissible rescalings of ±ω), in the form with a positive bound c.

Hypotheses: c > 0, M(X) ≠ ∞, and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x, where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. Admissible rescalings. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. Since 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a real submodule, sω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), so tsupport(sω) ⊆ U. Pointwise (sω)(x) = s·ω(x), and the coefficients of sα are s times those of α, so |sα| = |s|·|α|. Hence |(sω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and sω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U.
2. Mass bound. M(X) = X.massOn U is the supremum of ofReal(X(φ)) over admissible φ, so ofReal(X(sω)) ≤ M(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since M(X) ≠ ∞, this gives X(sω) ≤ M(X).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
3. Linearity and both signs. X(sω) = s·X(ω). With s = c⁻¹, then multiplying by c > 0: X(ω) ≤ c·M(X).toReal. With s = −c⁻¹: −X(ω) ≤ c·M(X).toReal. So |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal (abs_le). ∎
proof_key_steps: ±c⁻¹ω are admissible for M(X), since |sα| = |s||α|.
le_massOn and M(X) ≠ ∞ give ±c⁻¹X(ω) ≤ M(X).toReal.
Multiply by c > 0 and combine both signs.

subproblems.title: A linear functional bounded by c·A on forms with |ω| ≤ c is a current (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map (TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) and A ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), c ∈ ℝ, c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then there is a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (A : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |L ω| ≤ c * A) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
This accepted declaration is reused verbatim (byte-identical frozen type). The proof below proves its exact statement. Source: parent proof, step 0(b), converse part: a linear functional bounded by a multiple of the sup norm is a current. If ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, the 0-th derivatives converge uniformly, so ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and L(ω_j) → 0.

Hypothesis: |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. A ≥ 0. Take ω = 0 and c = 1: 0 = |L(0)| ≤ A.
2. Comparison of norms. For an n-covector α, |α| ≤ c₀‖α‖ with c₀ := √(P^n): each coefficient satisfies |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖, and there are at most P^n index maps.
3. Sup norms tend to 0. Let ω_j → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges. Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ω_j → 0 uniformly on K for every m. For m = 0 this says ω_j → 0 uniformly on K, since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖. So s_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0 (take s_j = 0 if K is empty). Off K, ω_j(x) = 0. Hence |ω_j(x)| ≤ c₀s_j for all x.
4. Sequential continuity. Put c_j := c₀s_j + 1/(j+1) > 0. Then |ω_j(x)| ≤ c_j for all x, so |L(ω_j)| ≤ c_j·A by hypothesis. Since c_j → 0 and A ≥ 0, L(ω_j) → 0.
5. Conclusion. L is ℝ-linear and satisfies the continuity condition of GeometricCurrentOn U n. So Y := ⟨L, step 4⟩ is a current with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coefficient norm ≤ √(P^n)·operator norm.
Test-form convergence to 0 gives uniform convergence of the forms themselves, so the sup norms tend to 0.
The hypothesis then gives L(ω_j) → 0, which is the continuity required of a current.

These are the test forms ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n: smooth, compactly supported in U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, called admissible for M_G. Neither U nor G is assumed open.

subproblems.natural_proof:
This accepted declaration is reused verbatim (byte-identical frozen type). The proof below proves its exact statement. Source: parent proof, step 0(c): (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(−ω) and −ω is admissible, so M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y). Here it is stated for an arbitrary region G.

1. Negatives are admissible. Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n G. Then −ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω ⊆ G. Also |(−ω)(x)| = |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). So −ω is admissible.
2. Splitting. (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω) by linearity. Hence ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A(ω)) + ofReal(B(−ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, applied to ω and to −ω).
3. Supremum. M_G(A − B) is the supremum of ofReal((A − B)(ω)) over admissible ω, so sSup_le gives M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). ∎
proof_key_steps: −ω is admissible whenever ω is.
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: Support criterion: vanishing off a compact K gives compact spt F ⊆ K (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

proof_key_steps: Each y ∈ U ∖ K has a ball with compact closure in U ∖ K on which F vanishes, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K.
spt F = K ∖ Z(F) with Z(F) open, so spt F is compact.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (slice forms η^ω_t and β^ω_s are test forms with ‖η^ω_t‖, ‖β^ω_s‖ ≤ ‖ω‖ and depend continuously on t) and step 0(e) (pointwise algebra by the covector bounds (L1), (L2)), specialized to the exact statement.
- (CB) is the antecedent of the statement.
- The derivative restriction γ_t is the parent's ∂_tβ^ω_t, written in covector form (Dω(ι(t, x))e₀)∘J.
- The parent's sup-norm continuity of t ↦ η_t (from uniform continuity of ω) is stated here in the stronger Lipschitz form. It comes from the reused sibling coeff_lipschitz (cbrld_cone_testForm_coeff_lipschitz).

Notation as in the statement; ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm of vectors and the operator norm of linear maps. SimonGMT affinePullbackForm L b θ is the form x ↦ θ(b + Lx).compContinuousLinearMap L.

1. The embedding J. Let J : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1}, J v := (0, v_1, …, v_N) (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp v))).
   (a) J is linear (compare coordinates with Fin.cases), and ‖Jv‖² = 0² + Σ_i v_i² = ‖v‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ). So J is a continuous linear isometry and ‖J‖ ≤ 1 (opNorm_le_bound).
   (b) Comparing coordinates (index 0 gives t, index i+1 gives x_i): ι(t, x) = single(0, t) + Jx, where single(0, t) := EuclideanSpace.single 0 t.
   (c) For fixed t, A_t(x) := single(0, t) + Jx satisfies dist(A_t x, A_t y) = ‖J(x − y)‖ = dist(x, y). So A_t is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a proper map (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, IsClosedEmbedding.isProperMap).
   (d) dist(ι(s, x), ι(t, x)) = dist(single(0, s), single(0, t)) = |s − t|, and ‖e₀‖ = 1.

2. The slice map S. For a (k+1)-covector α on ℝ^{N+1} put S(α) := (α.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J.
   (a) S(α)(v_1, …, v_k) = α(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) (curryLeft_apply_apply, with Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons).
   (b) S is additive and homogeneous: check on every v.
   (c) Bound: |S(α)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|α.curryLeft e₀| by (L1) with A = J; then ≤ |α.curryLeft e₀|, since 0 ≤ ‖J‖^k ≤ 1 and |·| ≥ 0; then ≤ ‖e₀‖·|α| = |α| by (L2) with v = e₀.

3. (A1). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and let ω₁(y) := ω(y).curryLeft e₀.
   (a) α ↦ α.curryLeft e₀ is continuous linear: it is evaluation at e₀ composed with the linear isometry ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI. So ω₁ is C^∞.
   (b) ω₁(y) = 0 whenever ω(y) = 0, so ω₁ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left).
   (c) Put η_t := affinePullbackForm J (single(0, t)) ω₁. By SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm (A_t is proper, step 1(c)), η_t is smooth with compact support. Also tsupport η_t ⊆ univ, so η_t ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
   (d) By definition and step 1(b), η_t(x) = ω₁(single(0, t) + Jx).compContinuousLinearMap J = S(ω(ι(t, x))). By step 2(a), η_t(x)(v) = ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k). This is (A1).

4. Normal form. Let η be any family satisfying the slice formula. For all t, x the covectors η_t(x) and S(ω(ι(t, x))) agree on every v (slice formula and step 2(a)). Hence η_t(x) = S(ω(ι(t, x))) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).

5. (A2). By coeff_lipschitz applied to ω (P = N+1, U = univ), choose c ≥ 0 with |ω(y) − ω(y')| ≤ c·dist(y, y') for all y, y'. The constant c depends only on ω, so it is fixed before η. Let η satisfy the slice formula.
   (i) By steps 4 and 2(c), |η_t(x)| = |S(ω(ι(t, x)))| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))|.
   (ii) By step 4 and step 2(b), η_s(x) − η_t(x) = S(ω(ι(s, x)) − ω(ι(t, x))). By steps 2(c) and 1(d), |η_s(x) − η_t(x)| ≤ |ω(ι(s, x)) − ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c·dist(ι(s, x), ι(t, x)) = c|s − t|.
   (iii) Fix t. The set F_t := {x : ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω} = A_t^{-1}(tsupport ω) is closed, because tsupport ω is closed and A_t is continuous. If x ∉ F_t, then ω(ι(t, x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so η_t(x) = S(0) = 0 by step 4. Thus support η_t ⊆ F_t, and tsupport η_t = closure(support η_t) ⊆ F_t (closure_minimal).

6. (B1), (B2). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}).
   (a) β_s := affinePullbackForm J (single(0, s)) ω is a test form on ℝ^N by affinePullbackForm_isTestForm. It satisfies β_s(x)(v) = ω(single(0, s) + Jx)(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv).
   (b) The form ω'(y) := Dω(y)e₀ is C^∞: y ↦ Dω(y) is C^∞ because ω is (ContDiff.fderiv_right), and it is followed by the continuous linear evaluation at e₀.
   (c) ω' has compact support: Dω vanishes outside tsupport ω (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), then use comp_left.
   (d) γ_t := affinePullbackForm J (single(0, t)) ω' is a test form with γ_t(x)(v) = ω'(ι(t, x))(Jv) = (Dω(ι(t, x))e₀)(Jv_1, …, Jv_k).

7. (B3). If β satisfies the formula of (B1), then β_s(x) = ω(ι(s, x)).compContinuousLinearMap J (ext). So |β_s(x)| ≤ ‖J‖^k·|ω(ι(s, x))| ≤ |ω(ι(s, x))| by (L1) and 0 ≤ ‖J‖ ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: J v = (0, v) is a linear isometry with ‖J‖ ≤ 1, ι(t, x) = single(0, t) + Jx, each x ↦ ι(t, x) is proper, and dist(ι(s, x), ι(t, x)) = |s − t|.
S(α) := (α.curryLeft e₀)∘J satisfies S(α)(v) = α(e₀, Jv) and |S(α)| ≤ |α| by (L1), (L2).
η_t := affine pull-back of ι_{e₀}ω along x ↦ ι(t, x) is a test form satisfying the slice formula.
Every slice family equals S(ω(ι(t, x))) pointwise, which gives the bound, the Lipschitz estimate (via coeff_lipschitz) and the support inclusion.
β_s and γ_t are affine pull-backs of ω and of Dω(·)e₀; (L1) gives |β_s(x)| ≤ |ω(ι(s, x))|.

Source: parent proof, step 5, first paragraph. It takes the coordinate formula for d with w_0 = e₀, w_i = Jv_i and applies the chain rule through x ↦ ι(t, x); the result is the identity (*) η^{dω}_t = ∂_tβ^ω_t − d(η^ω_t), stated here pointwise with ∂_tβ^ω_t(x)(v) = (Dω(ι(t, x))e₀)(Jv). Part (b) is the degree-0 remark of step 5.

Notation as in the statement. removeNth_i w is the tuple w with entry i deleted (Fin.removeNth).

1. Coordinate formula. Let θ be a form differentiable at y and w = (w_0, …, w_m). Then dθ(y)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·D[θ(·)(removeNth_i w)](y)(w_i) (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply = Mathlib extDeriv_apply).

2. Derivative of an evaluation. Let θ be differentiable at y and u a fixed tuple. Then D[θ(·)(u)](y)(h) = (Dθ(y)h)(u) for every h, since θ(·)(u) is θ followed by the continuous linear evaluation at u (fderiv_continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const and ContinuousLinearMap.flipAlternating_apply_apply).

3. The affine map. J v := (0, v) is continuous linear, and ι(t, x) = single(0, t) + Jx (compare coordinates). So for fixed t, A_t := ι(t, ·) is affine with derivative J at every point.

4. Chain rule for the slice. Fix t and a k-tuple u.
   (a) By the slice formula, x ↦ η_t(x)(u) and (y ↦ ω(y)(e₀, Ju_1, …, Ju_k)) ∘ A_t are equal as functions.
   (b) ω is C^∞ (a test form), so y ↦ ω(y)(e₀, Ju) is differentiable (step 2).
   (c) By the chain rule, D[η_t(·)(u)](x)(h) = D[ω(·)(e₀, Ju)](ι(t, x))(Jh) for every h ∈ ℝ^N.

5. Part (a). Let y := ι(t, x) and w := (e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_{k+1}) = Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v), so m = k+1. Split the sum of step 1 for θ = ω into i = 0 and i = j+1, j = 0, …, k (Fin.sum_univ_succ).
   (a) i = 0: removeNth_0 w = (Jv_1, …, Jv_{k+1}) and w_0 = e₀ (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_zero). By step 2 the term is (Dω(y)e₀)(Jv_1, …, Jv_{k+1}).
   (b) i = j+1: removeNth_{j+1} w = (e₀, J(removeNth_j v)) (Fin.cons_comp_succ_succAbove) and w_{j+1} = Jv_{j+1} (Fin.cons_succ). By step 4 with u = removeNth_j v and h = v_{j+1}, the term is (−1)^{j+1}·D[η_t(·)(removeNth_j v)](x)(v_{j+1}).
   (c) η_t is a test form, hence differentiable at x. Step 1 for θ = η_t with m = k gives d(η_t)(x)(v) = Σ_{j=0}^{k} (−1)^j·D[η_t(·)(removeNth_j v)](x)(v_{j+1}).
   (d) Since (−1)^{j+1} = −(−1)^j, the terms in (b) sum to −d(η_t)(x)(v). Hence dω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) = (Dω(ι(t, x))e₀)(Jv) − d(η_t)(x)(v).

6. Part (b). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}) and w = (e₀), so m = 0 and the sum of step 1 has only the term i = 0. So dω(y)(e₀) = D[ω(·)(removeNth_0 w)](y)(e₀) = (Dω(y)e₀)(removeNth_0 w) by step 2. Finally removeNth_0 w and J ∘ v are both the empty tuple, hence equal. ∎

subproblems.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus under a finite-mass current: ∫₀¹ X(γ_t) dt = X(β₁) − X(β₀)
subproblems.statement: Assume (REP), the representation antecedent of the selected statement (its exact frozen type): for all P, n, U open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U there are a measure μ on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and n-covectors α, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and, if also M_W(∂T) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn) for every open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0. Write ι(t, x) := (t, x_1, …, x_N) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))), e₀ := (1, 0, …, 0) (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1), Jv := ι(0, v), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, Dω := fderiv ℝ ω, and 𝒟^k(ℝ^m) := TestFormOn univ k (smooth compactly supported k-forms on ℝ^m). Let N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k with M(X) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}), and let β, γ : ℝ → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) satisfy β_s(x)(v) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) and γ_t(x)(v) = (Dω(ι(t, x))e₀)(Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all s, t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N and v ∈ (ℝ^N)^k. Then ∫_0^1 X(γ_t) dt = X(β_1) − X(β_0), the integral being the interval integral with respect to Lebesgue measure.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5, 'First integral (A0, Fubini, fundamental theorem of calculus)', together with step 0(d) (A0: (REP) represents a finite-mass current by μ and ξ). It is stated here for arbitrary families β, γ with the given formulas; γ_t is the parent's ∂_tβ^ω_t.
- (REP) is the antecedent of the statement.
- The uniform bound uses conjunct (iv) of the reused sibling coeff_norm (regcomp_covectorEuclideanNorm_seminorm_retract).

Notation as in the statement. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms. M^ℝ := M(X).toReal.

1. Representation (A0).
   (a) For every open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^N, M_W(X) ≤ M_{ℝ^N}(X) = M(X) < ∞ (massOn_mono).
   (b) So (REP) with P = N, n = k, U = univ (open) gives μ and ξ : ℝ^N → MultiVector N k with: M_W(X) = μ(W) for open W; ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α; and X(φ) = ∫ ξ(x)(φ(x)) dμ for every φ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
   (c) Taking W = ℝ^N gives μ(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞, so μ is a finite measure.

2. Normal forms. Let J v := (0, v) as in slice_forms; then ι(t, x) = t e₀ + Jx. Let C_J : α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap J be the continuous linear map from k-covectors on ℝ^{N+1} to k-covectors on ℝ^N (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM). Comparing values on every v (ext), the hypotheses give β_s(x) = C_J(ω(s e₀ + Jx)) and γ_t(x) = C_J(Dω(t e₀ + Jx)e₀) for all s, t, x.

3. Regularity of ω. ω is C^∞ with compact support. So ω is differentiable and Dω is continuous. Both ω and y ↦ Dω(y)e₀ are continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence bounded: ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M₀ and ‖Dω(y)e₀‖ ≤ M₁ for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

4. Derivative in t. Fix x. The map t ↦ t e₀ + Jx has derivative e₀, so t ↦ ω(t e₀ + Jx) has derivative Dω(t e₀ + Jx)e₀ (chain rule, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt). Composing with the continuous linear maps C_J and ξ(x) and using step 2, f_x(t) := ξ(x)(β_t(x)) has derivative ξ(x)(γ_t(x)) at every t ∈ ℝ.

5. Continuity and bounds.
   (a) (t, x) ↦ γ_t(x) = C_J(Dω(t e₀ + Jx)e₀) is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^N, and x ↦ β_s(x) is continuous for each s.
   (b) By coeff_norm (iv) there is c > 0 with |α| ≤ c‖α‖ for every k-covector α on ℝ^N.
   (c) Hence |ξ(x)(γ_t(x))| ≤ |γ_t(x)| ≤ c‖C_J‖M₁ and |ξ(x)(β_s(x))| ≤ c‖C_J‖M₀ for all t, s, x.

6. Measurability and integrability. Let λ be Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, 1], a finite measure.
   (a) The pairing (α, L) ↦ L(α) on (k-covectors) × MultiVector N k is continuous.
   (b) Since ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, (t, x) ↦ ξ(x) is a.e. strongly measurable for λ ⊗ μ (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd). (t, x) ↦ γ_t(x) is continuous, hence strongly measurable.
   (c) So G(t, x) := ξ(x)(γ_t(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for λ ⊗ μ (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂). G is bounded (step 5) and λ ⊗ μ is finite, so G is λ ⊗ μ-integrable (Integrable.of_bound).
   (d) In the same way, x ↦ ξ(x)(β_s(x)) is μ-integrable for each s.

7. Conclusion.
   (a) ∫_0^1 X(γ_t) dt = ∫_0^1 ∫ ξ(x)(γ_t(x)) dμ(x) dt, by step 1.
   (b) = ∫ ∫_0^1 ξ(x)(γ_t(x)) dt dμ(x), by Fubini (integral_integral_swap), using ∫_0^1 = ∫_{(0,1]} (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le) and step 6.
   (c) = ∫ [ξ(x)(β_1(x)) − ξ(x)(β_0(x))] dμ(x), by the fundamental theorem of calculus for f_x (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt). Its derivative (step 4) is continuous in t by step 5, hence interval integrable.
   (d) = ∫ ξ(x)(β_1(x)) dμ − ∫ ξ(x)(β_0(x)) dμ, by integral_sub and step 6.
   (e) = X(β_1) − X(β_0), by step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: (REP) with U = univ represents X by a finite measure μ and a bounded measurable orientation ξ.
β_s(x) = C_J(ω(s e₀ + Jx)) and γ_t(x) = C_J(Dω(t e₀ + Jx)e₀), so t ↦ ξ(x)(β_t(x)) has derivative ξ(x)(γ_t(x)).
Uniform bounds (coeff_norm (iv), compact support) and a.e. strong measurability make ξ(x)(γ_t(x)) integrable on (0, 1] × ℝ^N.
Fubini, the fundamental theorem of calculus for each x, and the representation again give X(β_1) − X(β_0).

Source: parent proof, step 2 (definition cyl(X)(ω) := ∫_0^1 X(η^ω_t) dt, continuity of the integrand, linearity, the bound |cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖, current property and M(cyl X) ≤ M(X)) and step 4 (support).
- Step 1 of the parent is supplied by the sibling slice_forms.
- 0(b) is supplied by the reused siblings abs_le_mass (cmc_fc_sc_abs_le_mul_mass) and bounded_current (cmc_fc_sc_current_of_coeff_bound).
- 0(c)(S1) is supplied by the reused sibling support_vanish (rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish).
- (CB) and (VO) are the antecedents; (CB) is passed to slice_forms.

A slice family of ω is a family η : ℝ → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with η_t(x)(v) = ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) for all t, x, v. M^ℝ := M(X).toReal ≥ 0.

1. Slice families. By slice_forms (A1), choose for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) a slice family η^ω. Any two slice families η, η' of the same ω are equal: η_t(x)(v) = η'_t(x)(v) for all t, x, v, so η_t(x) = η'_t(x) (ext), and η_t = η'_t in 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) (Subtype.ext, funext).

2. Continuity of t ↦ X(η_t). Let η be a slice family of ω and c ≥ 0 the constant of slice_forms (A2) for ω.
   (a) For s, t and ε > 0, the test form η_s − η_t satisfies |(η_s − η_t)(x)| = |η_s(x) − η_t(x)| ≤ c|s − t| ≤ c|s − t| + ε for all x, by (A2)(ii).
   (b) Since c|s − t| + ε > 0 and M(X) ≠ ∞, abs_le_mass gives |X(η_s) − X(η_t)| = |X(η_s − η_t)| ≤ (c|s − t| + ε)·M^ℝ.
   (c) Letting ε ↓ 0, |X(η_s) − X(η_t)| ≤ c·M^ℝ·|s − t|. So t ↦ X(η_t) is Lipschitz, hence continuous.

3. The functional L. Define L(ω) := ∫_0^1 X(η^ω_t) dt.
   (a) The slice formula is linear in ω. So for ω, ω' and a ∈ ℝ, t ↦ η^ω_t + η^{ω'}_t is a slice family of ω + ω' and t ↦ a·η^ω_t is one of aω. By step 1, η^{ω+ω'}_t = η^ω_t + η^{ω'}_t and η^{aω}_t = a·η^ω_t.
   (b) X is linear, and the integrands are continuous (step 2), hence interval integrable. So L(ω + ω') = L(ω) + L(ω') and L(aω) = a·L(ω): L is ℝ-linear.

4. Bound. Let c > 0 with |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. By slice_forms (A2)(i), |η^ω_t(x)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c for all t, x. So |X(η^ω_t)| ≤ c·M^ℝ by abs_le_mass, and |L(ω)| ≤ c·M^ℝ·|1 − 0| = c·M^ℝ (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const).

5. The current, and (c). By bounded_current (P = N+1, n = k+1, U = univ, A = M^ℝ) and step 4, there is Y ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for all ω. If η is any slice family of ω, then η = η^ω (step 1), so Y(ω) = ∫_0^1 X(η_t) dt, and t ↦ X(η_t) is continuous (step 2). This is (c).

6. Mass, (a). M(Y) = M_univ(Y) is the supremum of ofReal(Y(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For such ω, step 4 with c = 1 gives Y(ω) = L(ω) ≤ |L(ω)| ≤ M^ℝ. So ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(M^ℝ) = M(X), since M(X) < ∞. Taking the supremum (sSup_le), M(Y) ≤ M(X).

7. Support, (b). Assume spt X is compact and let E := {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X}.
   (a) E is the image of the compact set [0, 1] × spt X under the continuous map (t, x) ↦ ι(t, x) (coordinates t, x_1, …, x_N), so E is compact.
   (b) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, and t ∈ [0, 1]. By slice_forms (A2)(iii), tsupport η^ω_t ⊆ {x : ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω}. If some x ∈ tsupport η^ω_t also lay in spt X, then ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, which is impossible.
   (c) So tsupport η^ω_t is disjoint from spt X, and X(η^ω_t) = 0 by (VO) (P = N, n = k, U = univ, S = X).
   (d) The integrand vanishes on [0, 1] = uIcc 0 1, so Y(ω) = L(ω) = ∫_0^1 0 dt = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr).
   (e) By support_vanish (U = univ open, K = E compact ⊆ univ), spt Y ⊆ E and spt Y is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: Slice families exist (slice_forms (A1)) and are unique; t ↦ X(η_t) is Lipschitz by (A2)(ii) and abs_le_mass.
L(ω) := ∫_0^1 X(η^ω_t) dt is linear, and |L(ω)| ≤ c·M(X) whenever |ω| ≤ c ((A2)(i) and abs_le_mass).
bounded_current turns L into a current Y; testing admissible forms gives M(Y) ≤ M(X).
Forms missing E = ι([0, 1] × spt X) have slices missing spt X, so (VO) kills the integrand and support_vanish gives a compact spt Y ⊆ E.
